samples.summary: `--dry-run` now prints a URL that is not the URL that would be sent (bypasses the new `seg()`)
samples.evidence: `printDryRun` builds `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${config.workspace}${path}` with the raw workspace and the raw ids the command interpolated (e.g. `cells.ts:55` builds `/documents/${docId}/tabs/${tab}/cells/${ref}` unencoded), while every real request now goes through `seg()` in http-client.ts:71 (encodeURIComponent + refusal of `.`/`..`). So for any id containing `/`, `%`, `#`, `?` or a space the preview URL differs from the issued one, and `wafflebase docs delete .. --dry-run` prints a perfectly normal-looking request that the non-dry-run path refuses outright with `Invalid path segment`. docs/design/cli.md:811 states dry-run "prints the request that would be sent", and tabs.ts:34-37 states the repo's own rule that a dry run printing something the server would reject is worse than no dry run. Fix: have the dry-run printer share the same segment builder.

samples.summary: `clampUpstreamText` discards any upstream message whose first non-space character is `<`, losing the only diagnostic text for legitimate messages
samples.evidence: `if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith('<')) return null;` treats a leading `<` as proof the body is an HTML document. A real Nest/class-validator message such as `"<stdin> is not a valid source"` or `"<id> must be a UUID"` (and a class-validator array whose first joined element starts with `<`) is silently replaced by a bare `HTTP <status>`, which is exactly the information loss the rest of this helper is written to avoid. A cheap tightening (`/^<(!doctype|html)/i`, or requiring a closing `>` plus length) would keep real messages.

samples.summary: The 4 KB stderr bound is measured on compact JSON but the bytes actually written are pretty-printed, so the real output can be several times the documented bound
samples.evidence: `safeEnvelope` decides with `JSON.stringify(whole).length <= MAX_UPSTREAM_BODY` (no indent), while both emitters print `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` (formatter.ts:225 and :250). A deeply nested 3,999-character compact envelope expands to well over 4 KB — often 2-3x — once indented, so the stated "serialized body stays under 4 KB" guarantee (README/design-doc table) does not hold for the bytes on stderr. Measure the same string that is printed.

samples.summary: `isErrorEnvelope` accepts an empty-string `code`, so an agent can be handed `{"error":{"code":""}}` from the forwarding path while the throwing path guarantees a non-empty code
samples.evidence: `typeof (err as {code?: unknown}).code === 'string'` is true for `''`, and `safeEnvelope` then forwards `code: ''.slice(0,80) === ''`. The sibling classifier `errorCode()` (formatter.ts:44) deliberately requires `code.length > 0` before trusting a code. The whole point of the change is that the `code` an agent branches on is always meaningful; an empty code defeats that for a malformed upstream body that would otherwise fall through to `HTTP_ERROR`.

samples.summary: `seg()` throws a bare `Error` with no `code`, so a refused dot-segment id surfaces as the generic `ERROR` code the change is otherwise trying to eliminate
samples.evidence: `throw new Error(`Invalid path segment: "${value}"`)` has no `code` property, so `errorCode()` (formatter.ts:41-47) falls back to `'ERROR'`. Every other CLI-side rejection in this change carries a stable code (`HTTP_ERROR`, `CONFIRMATION_REQ`, `INVALID_RESPONSE`), and docs/design/cli.md's §10 code table does not list this condition at all, so an agent that hits `wafflebase docs get ..` gets an undocumented, unbranchable code.
searchedFor: docs/design/cli.md grep for 'segment'/'Invalid path' — no matches

samples.evidence: `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes) { io.stderr(upstreamErrorJson(res)); }` passes a *successful* response into a helper that formats `HTTP ${res.status}`, producing `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 200"}}` for a 200 that carried no bytes. Before the change the same branch printed `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}` with no misleading status text. Worth splitting the empty-body case out with its own message.
